subject: Why do I get different pvalues of estimates when running standardizedsolution(fit, type = "std.lv")?

messages.author: 418b1edcfb01d257
messages.subject: Why do I get different pvalues of estimates when running standardizedsolution(fit, type = "std.lv")?
parts:
I seem to be getting different pvalues for certain estimates on correlated latent variables when I run it with parameterestimates(fit, standardised = TRUE) vs standardizedsolution(fit, type = "std.lv").

See below for code and output. As an example, RIpb ~~ RIsi are not significant via the parameterestimates approach, whereas they are under the standardizedsolution.

Thanks in advance for your help.

-----


.fit_corr_mod <-
  parameterestimates(riclpm_fit, standardized = TRUE) %>%
  select(lhs, op, rhs, std.all, pvalue) %>%
  filter(op %in% "~~")

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Why do I get different pvalues of estimates when running standardizedsolution(fit, type = "std.lv")?
parts: I seem to be getting different pvalues for certain estimates on correlated latent variables when I run it with parameterestimates(fit, standardised = TRUE) vs standardizedsolution(fit, type = "std.lv").

parameterEstimates() returns tests for unstandardized parameters.  standardizedSolution() returns tests for standardized parameters.  They are not the same because standardized parameters are scaled by additional estimated quantities, e.g., b*_yx = b_yx * (sd_x / sd_y).  I think the SEs for standardized parameters essentially use the delta method.
